what_it_is: A system of NFC- and radio-enabled ESP32 wristbands for event attendees. Capital One Nessie account per attendee funds merch purchases and receives claim payouts.
Per-band page with zone history, ranked people met with socials, booths visited, tagged photos.

what_it_is: Sunglasses with an ESP32-CAM, two time-of-flight sensors and two servo pads, paired with a laptop-controlled DJI Tello drone. The user asks by voice for an item or person, the drone finds it and returns, and the glasses guide the user there with speech and haptic pads.

Face ID against one photo per teammate lets the drone look for people by name.
Computes the object's position relative to where the wearer stood and faced, using monocular depth and pose.
Spoken directions via TTS in AirPods plus two servo pads on the glasses indicate direction; ToF sensors on glasses.
Drone steering uses a 1,446-neuron subgraph from a fly connectome with a 34-parameter adapter trained by CMA-ES on Modal.

what_it_is: A drop-in Fill with Formly button for business forms. A popup lets the user upload files or connect Google, iCloud or T-Mobile, builds a private fact profile (digital twin), fills the form with per-field sources, and returns only the answers the user approves.

Ask every time, auto-share basics, or share everything; sensitive fields such as SSN need explicit allow once, always or deny.
File upload live; Google and iCloud are mock sign-ins with persona data; T-Mobile mock sign-in calls the real sandbox API.
T-Mobile signup, SpaceXAI job application, Chase card and California DMV, filled for nine synthetic personas.

what_it_is: A local privacy layer between clinical-trial staff and cloud LLMs. It strips HIPAA identifiers and sensitive trial details on-device, routes each request to an abstract rewrite, a differentially-private proxy, or local-only answering, then re-applies the original entities to the cloud reply. Hidden-state embeddings clipped and Gaussian-noised with Renyi accounting, per-session budget and hard refusal when exhausted.
Cloud response is returned locally and placeholders restored longest-key-first.
Five attacks (span inversion, similarity, membership inference, etc.) measure text-surface leakage per route over a 1,200-document synthetic corpus.

what_it_is: A mechanistic-interpretability experiment asking whether instruction-tuned LLMs track an object's location as it moves through templated stories, and whether failures come from never encoding the answer or from failing to read it out. Linear probes on residual-stream activations are compared with model outputs.
problem_and_user: ML researchers and builders of narrative-understanding systems who need to know whether state-tracking failures are storage or readout problems.

Per-layer probes test whether the correct location is encoded; Gemma 2B probes reach 55.4 percent vs 41.3 percent output.
Compares 2B and 7B: 2B signal rises from layer 7, 7B jumps after layer 17; repo extends to nine models.

what_it_is: A Python heuristic optimizer that fills a warehouse floor with racking bays, respecting columns, uneven ceilings and walls, scored on cost versus capacity. Parallel workers pack from different corners within a 30-second limit; a Streamlit viewer lets users inspect and tweak layouts.
problem_and_user: Warehouse planners laying out storage bays in irregular spaces for maximum capacity at lowest cost (Mecalux challenge).

core_features.how_it_works: Reads perimeter, obstacles, ceiling profile and bay catalog; repo includes public test cases.
A priority queue seeded from corners and obstacle edges proposes spots; the most cost-efficient bay is tried first, then a 180-degree flip.
A rotation is kept if it lines the bay's gap up with an existing aisle, yielding face-to-face or back-to-back rows.
Polygons are shrunk 1 mm before overlap tests so bays can touch edge to edge.
One worker per CPU core uses a different gravity direction; run stops at about 27 s to return a valid layout.
Price-to-load ratio raised to a power that penalises low area usage.
Streamlit and Plotly app with layers, captions, score metrics, and a list for moving or deleting bays.

what_it_is: A C++ warehouse bay-placement solver for the Mecalux challenge using fast construction, hill climbing and simulated annealing with parallel restarts, plus a React UI that loads the CSV inputs, runs the solver through an Express bridge and shows 2D and 3D results.

Q equals price per load raised to 2 minus bay area over free area; lower is better; UI scoring mirrors the solver.
Warehouse, obstacles, ceiling and bay type CSVs in, solution CSV out.

what_it_is: An agent-evaluation platform for multi-agent orchestration: a graph and Gantt trace viewer, statistical A/B comparison of harnesses, and a meta-agent that writes and tests new harness variants. Built on Inspect AI and OpenHands.

Multi++ (12 specialists), Kim-Gate delegation gate, Structured-Delegation, Cross-Sibling-Discovery bus, and a stock baseline.

Public uAgent on Agentverse (chat and payment protocols) spawns participant agents; demo is a 50-agent simplified economy.

what_it_is: A Python program that captures live audio, turns frequency, amplitude and phase into rotations on 12 simulated qubits via Qiskit, and renders the quantum state as waves and particles in OpenGL. A small PyTorch network scores musical intensity to change the visuals.
problem_and_user: No problem framed; an experimental audiovisual piece for people curious about sound and quantum mechanics.

core_features.how_it_works: PyAudio reads the device output (virtual device such as BlackHole) with selectable input; samples frequency, amplitude, phase every 16 ms over a 2 s window.
Amplitude sets rotation strength, frequency sets oscillation rate, phase shifts orientation; qubit groups in plus/minus, 0/1 and Y-basis states, entangled across groups.
PyTorch model trained on about 60 song samples outputs -1.0 to 1.0 intensity from the buffer.
OpenGL draws the transformed state as a wave, computed on a separate thread.
Particle color, speed, spread follow intensity: warm and fast when intense, cool and slow when soft.
Hand-built FFT features because existing libraries were too slow for real-time.

user_flow: Install dependencies and a virtual audio device
Run the main script
Play music
View waves and particles reacting; optionally project on a screen
